view://rgb.description: Provides view from robots RGB camera
view://rgb.name: RGB View

cancel_attention.description:
Stops attending to the person (the camera keeps its tilt; do_look levels it).
Returns the final attention status.
cancel_attention.name: cancel_attention

cancel_nav.description: Cancels the active navigation goal, stopping the robot within one step.
cancel_nav.name: cancel_nav

do_look.description:
Tilts the robot's camera, like the Kinect on the real robot. The camera sits about
0.3 m above the floor: level, it sees legs, furniture bases and the floor ahead. "up"
tilts it 27 degrees up to see faces, tabletops and what a person is doing; "straight"
levels it again. The tilt stays until changed, except that starting a drive levels the
camera. Returns the camera's new tilt, not a picture: call get_current_view to see.

Args:
    direction (LOOK_DIRECTION): "up" or "straight"
do_look.name: do_look

do_move.description:
Moves the agent ahead("MoveAhead"), back("MoveBack"), left("MoveLeft"), or right("MoveRight"). Returns a summary of result of moving.

Manual moves preempt (cancel) any active navigation goal, like nav2 teleop.

Example: do_move(action="MoveAhead", moveMagnitude=2) -> moves agent forward by 2 meters

Args:
    action (MOVE_ACTION): direction to move
    moveMagnitude (float, optional): how much to move by in meters. Defaults to 1..
do_move.name: do_move

do_rotate.description:
Rotates the agent left or right. Returns a summary of the result of rotating.

Manual rotations preempt (cancel) any active navigation goal, like nav2 teleop.

Example: do_rotate(action="RotateRight", degrees=45) -> rotates agent 45 degrees to the right

Args:
    action (ROTATE_ACTION): rotation direction/action (e.g. "RotateLeft" or "RotateRight")
    degrees (float, optional): how many degrees to rotate. Defaults to 90..
do_rotate.name: do_rotate

end_overhead_recording.description:
Stops the active overhead recording and finalizes the video.

Returns the absolute path of a browser-playable H.264 mp4 on the server's
filesystem plus duration and frame stats. Errors if no recording is
active.
end_overhead_recording.name: end_overhead_recording

get_attention_status.description:
The attention status without a picture (see set_attention): state, target, distance_m,
bearing_deg, seen_s, unseen_s, moving, tilt_deg, standoff_m, since_s, reason.
get_attention_status.name: get_attention_status

get_current_view.description:
Gets the robot's current camera view, annotated with selectable destinations.

Returns the RGB frame with numbered markers plus a JSON list of destinations:
visible objects (green boxes) and drivable passages detected from depth
(cyan boxes: doorways, hallways, wide openings that fit the robot). Pass any
destination "id" to set_nav_goal to drive there. Marker numbers restart each
view; ids are stable.
get_current_view.name: get_current_view

get_map.description:
Gets the top-down occupancy map the robot has built from its depth camera at camera
height, like a lidar SLAM map: unexplored grey, free space white, obstacles black. Overlaid:
robot pose (red triangle), remaining planned path (yellow), known destinations (dots), and
the active goal (star). Unexplored areas fill in as the robot looks around and drives.
get_map.name: get_map

get_nav_status.description:
Gets the state of the current/last navigation goal.

state is one of idle | planning | following | succeeded | canceled | failed;
progress holds distance traveled/remaining, percent, eta_s, and waypoint
counts while a goal exists. Poll this after set_nav_goal until a terminal
state (succeeded/canceled/failed).
get_nav_status.name: get_nav_status

list_destinations.description:
Lists every destination the robot has seen so far (across all views).

Ids remain valid for set_nav_goal: objects are re-resolved to their current
position; passages are fixed world waypoints.
list_destinations.name: list_destinations

set_attention.description:
Keeps a person in view in the background, like the robot's own reflex: it turns to
centre them (within 10 degrees), tilts the camera up when they are closer than 2 m and
level beyond 2.5 m, drives to about 1.3 m when they stand still farther than 1.8 m away,
and backs up when they are closer than 0.9 m. Only a person can be attended: pass the
Person destination id from get_current_view. Ends by itself after 5 s out of sight
("lost"), and whenever a drive (set_nav_goal) or manual control (do_move, do_rotate,
do_look) starts; an active drive is preempted when attention starts.

Returns the attention status, also inside every get_current_view as "attention":
state (off | aiming | approaching | framed | searching | lost), distance_m, bearing_deg
(positive = to the right), seen_s (in view for), unseen_s, moving, tilt_deg (camera),
standoff_m, since_s, reason (why it ended). "framed" means the view is centred on the
person with the right tilt: a good moment to call get_current_view and look.

Args:
    destination_id (str): the person's destination id, e.g. "obj:person_0"
    standoff_m (float): how close to stand, 0.7 to 2.0 m (default 1.3); it backs up when
        they are 0.4 m closer than that
    follow (bool): keep up with them when they walk off (approach a walking person too)
    greet (bool): once they are framed, wiggle (turn a little left, right and back): hello
set_attention.name: set_attention

set_nav_goal.description:
Plans a path to a destination and starts driving there in the background.

destination_id comes from get_current_view / list_destinations (e.g.
"obj:Fridge|-01.50|+00.00|-00.70" or "psg:1"). Returns immediately with the
planned path and ETA; poll get_nav_status for progress. An active goal is
preempted (canceled and replaced), like nav2.

Args:
    destination_id (str): id of the destination to drive to
    speed_mps (float, optional): driving speed in meters/second. Defaults to 0.35.
set_nav_goal.name: set_nav_goal

sim_camera_move.description:
Simulator only: fly the free camera and return its new frame (JPEG) and pose.

Args:
    forward, right, up: metres, relative to where the camera looks (forward/right stay
        level; up is world-vertical). Height is clamped to the room.
    yaw, pitch: degrees to turn (yaw) and tilt (pitch, positive looks down).
    zoom: degrees of field of view to remove (positive zooms in).
sim_camera_move.name: sim_camera_move

sim_camera_reset.description:
Simulator only: jump the free camera to a preset relative to the robot and return the
frame (JPEG) and pose. Presets: "chase" (behind and above, looking at the robot), "front"
(in front, looking back at it), "top" (straight down).
sim_camera_reset.name: sim_camera_reset

sim_camera_view.description:
Simulator only: the free camera's current frame (JPEG) and pose.

The free camera is a user-controlled third-party camera for watching the robot from
anywhere in the room. It is created at a chase viewpoint on first use. Not part of the
robot contract; robot brains must not use it.
sim_camera_view.name: sim_camera_view

sim_exploration_stats.description:
Simulator only: how much of the scene's floor the robot has explored so far.

coverage_pct: share of the scene's reachable positions (AI2-THOR's 0.25 m navigation grid)
that the occupancy map has seen as free floor. visited_pct: share within 0.5 m of the path
the robot has travelled. known_m2 / free_m2: area the map has observed / seen free.
trail_m: distance travelled. For experiments; not part of the robot contract (a real robot
has no ground-truth floor plan), and robot brains must not use it.
sim_exploration_stats.name: sim_exploration_stats

sim_person_activity.description:
Simulator only: the person does one thing, then stands idle. kind: ignore (wander,
keeping away from the robot), object (go to a piece of furniture and use it for
`seconds`: work at a table or shelf, watch the TV, sit on a sofa or chair; object_id
picks one), walk_by (pass the robot at arm's length without looking at it), interact
(come to the robot and try body language: style wave, beckon or crouch; if the robot
does not respond within patience_s they give up and leave). sim_person_state's
"activity" says what they are doing and whether they want the robot.
sim_person_activity.name: sim_person_activity

sim_person_despawn.description: Simulator only: remove the person (a borrowed body returns to where it was).
sim_person_despawn.name: sim_person_despawn

sim_person_gesture.description:
Simulator only: the person stops and shows body language for `seconds`, facing the
robot unless face_robot is false. kind: wave, beckon ("come here"), point, clap,
crouch, pet (crouch and reach out), use (work with both hands), sit, stand.
sim_person_gesture.name: sim_person_gesture

sim_person_goto.description:
Simulator only: walk the person to a world point along the reachable grid
(collision-checked steps; it yields when the robot is close).
sim_person_goto.name: sim_person_goto

sim_person_goto_robot.description: Simulator only: walk the person toward the robot, stopping about stop_m away.
sim_person_goto_robot.name: sim_person_goto_robot

sim_person_life.description:
Simulator only: the person lives procedurally, one activity after another, chosen at
random by weight (default ignore 0.3, object 0.3, walk_by 0.2, interact 0.2; see
sim_person_activity). A seed makes the day repeat exactly.
sim_person_life.name: sim_person_life

sim_person_move.description:
Simulator only: one manual collision-checked step relative to the person's
facing (teleop; preempts any route). Negative values go back/left.
sim_person_move.name: sim_person_move

sim_person_script.description:
Simulator only: a timed behaviour script for the person, e.g.
[{"at_s": 60, "action": "walk_past_robot", "args": {"clearance_m": 0.8}}].
The clock starts when the script is set. Actions: goto, goto_robot,
walk_past_robot, wander, stop, set_speed, face_robot, pause, gesture
({"kind", "seconds"}), activity ({"kind", "style", "seconds"}), life
({"enabled", "seed", "weights"}).
sim_person_script.name: sim_person_script

sim_person_set_speed.description: Simulator only: set the person's walking speed (0.1-1.5 m/s; default 0.6).
sim_person_set_speed.name: sim_person_set_speed

sim_person_spawn.description:
Simulator only: put a person into the scene; the robot then sees it as an
ordinary destination labeled "Person". Spawns at (x, z) snapped to the walkable
grid, or at the reachable spot farthest from the robot. body="" uses the
configured one (the humanoid asset, which needs the server started with
AI2THOR_MCP_PERSON_PRELOAD=1, or a borrowed objectType such as "Statue").
Not part of the robot contract; robot brains must not use it.
sim_person_spawn.name: sim_person_spawn

sim_person_state.description:
Simulator only: the person's pose, mode (off/idle/manual/goto/wander/script),
speed, remaining route, blocked reason, and the robot's pose and distance —
everything a driver (human or LLM) needs in one call.
sim_person_state.name: sim_person_state

sim_person_stop.description: Simulator only: stop the person where it stands (clears route, wander and script).
sim_person_stop.name: sim_person_stop

sim_person_turn.description: Simulator only: turn the person in place (positive = clockwise).
sim_person_turn.name: sim_person_turn

sim_person_walk_past_robot.description:
Simulator only: walk the person past the robot — to a spot ~1.5 m beyond it,
offset clearance_m to the side — the scripted "someone walks by" move.
sim_person_walk_past_robot.name: sim_person_walk_past_robot

sim_person_wander.description:
Simulator only: the person wanders between random reachable spots with short
dwell pauses. A seed makes the walk reproducible across runs.
sim_person_wander.name: sim_person_wander

start_overhead_recording.description:
Starts recording an overhead video of the robot.

Exactly one recording can be active at a time; starting while one is
active is an error. mode="follow" (default) keeps a top-down camera
hovering above the robot as it drives; mode="scene" fixes an orthographic
camera over the whole floor plan. The video is real time (idle gaps show
as held frames) and capped at 10 minutes. Call end_overhead_recording to
finalize and get the mp4 path (saved under data/recordings/ on the server
machine). Note: the overhead camera keeps rendering after the first
recording, adding a small cost to every subsequent step.

Args:
    mode (str, optional): "follow" or "scene". Defaults to "follow".
start_overhead_recording.name: start_overhead_recording
